text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000226 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, including on low-complexity patients, but documentation is too thin to say whether this is upcoding or a legitimately complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry mostly single symptom or follow-up diagnoses (e.g., R10.9 on C0116092, R21 on C0116456, J06.9 on C0117163, Z09 on C0116942) that would not usually suggest high-complexity decision-making. That is the concerning half of the pattern; the sampled high-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0116103, C0117060) look consistent with the billed level. The records review offers some counterweight but little power: all three documented 99215 notes support high MDM, including two on low-complexity patients (C0116937, C0117023), and no data-reviewed notes lacked a lab or test line, so there is no sign of cloned notes in this small sample. With records for only about 1% of claims, the reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here, checking whether the documented MDM reflects that visit's problems rather than templated text."}
